source_text: Tu utrumvis hic simpliciter confitere, et cavillari desine; aut dic nobiscum liberum esse arbitrium; et remove testimonium, quod suo tempore congrue prolatum est; aut, sicut in his libris, quos nunc per Alypium ad Bonifacium misisti, dic captivum esse arbitrium, quod nos liberum dicimus, et desine te negare Manichaeum.
pass_a_gloss: Confess here simply whichever you will, and cease to cavil; either say with us that choice is free; and remove the testimony, which was brought forth fittingly in its own time; or, as in these books, which you have now sent through Alypius to Boniface, say that choice is captive, which we say is free, and cease to deny that you are a Manichaean.

lemmas.lexica: LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: Simply acknowledge whichever of these you choose, then, and stop quibbling. Either say with us that choice is free, and remove the testimony that was appropriately spoken in its own setting, or say, as in those books you have now sent to Boniface through Alypius, that the choice we call free is captive, and stop denying that you are a Manichaean.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
